**RE: Member appeal of adverse benefit determination — ACL reconstruction (CPT 29888)**
**Member:** Rowan Ellison
**Member ID:** W486282210
**Reference number:** POC-5D5B151DE3-65694
**Date of denial notice:** 2026-08-17
**Plan:** Ambetter (WellCare), Commercial/ACA, North Carolina

---

To the Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing the denial of coverage for ACL reconstruction (CPT 29888), which Ambetter denied on 2026-08-17 under reference number POC-5D5B151DE3-65694. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision and to approve the procedure my surgeon has documented as necessary.

**A note on the plan's criteria, which have not been provided to me**

The denial notice tells me the decision was made under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria, but it does not name that policy or tell me what it requires. Because of that, I cannot quote the plan's own language back to it, and I am not going to guess at it. Nothing in this letter should be read as a quotation from any Ambetter policy — I have not been given one. I also understand that Ambetter delegates review of musculoskeletal surgery requests to TurningPoint, whose criteria are not published for members to read.

**My written request for the criteria used**

I am formally requesting, in writing, that Ambetter provide me with a free copy of the specific medical policy and clinical review criteria that were applied to this request — including any criteria applied by TurningPoint or another delegated reviewer on the plan's behalf — along with the credentials of the reviewer who made the determination. The plan holds these documents; I do not. If my records are said to fall short of a standard for conservative treatment, I am asking the plan to state that standard in writing: what treatments it requires, for how long, and over what period. I cannot meaningfully respond to a requirement that has not been disclosed to me, and I ask that the plan supply it as part of this appeal.

**What my records actually document**

The reason given for the denial is that the records do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery. Here is what the records submitted with the prior authorization actually show:

- **Symptom duration.** I have had 14 months of progressive pain in the knee, which has not been relieved by rest.
- **Supervised physical therapy and bracing.** I completed 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy for range of motion and quadriceps strengthening, with bracing, from 2026-03-27 to 2026-07-03 — 20 visits in total. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication.** I took NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief.
- **Injection.** I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-28, which gave me about 2 weeks of partial relief.
- **Imaging.** An MRI of the knee on 2026-07-01 showed a complete mid-substance tear of the anterior cruciate ligament with a bone bruise pattern. The menisci are intact and there is no significant arthritis.
- **Function.** I have recurrent instability with pivoting, and my knee has given way twice on stairs.
- **Exam.** Provocative testing on the affected side is positive, and my range of motion is limited by pain.
- **Surgical readiness.** I have no active infection and no untreated substance use, my BMI is 29, and I do not smoke.

That is a documented course of supervised physical therapy with bracing, an anti-inflammatory medication trial, and an injection — all tried before surgery was requested, and all recorded in the chart. My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, an orthopedic surgeon, has documented that the reconstruction is needed.

I would also note plainly that the MRI shows the ligament is completely torn. Therapy, bracing, medication, and injection were tried anyway, over a period of months, and my knee continues to give way.

**What I am asking for**

I ask that Ambetter overturn the denial dated 2026-08-17 and authorize ACL reconstruction (CPT 29888) as requested by Dr. Okafor. If the plan upholds the denial in whole or in part, I ask that it send me a written explanation that identifies the specific criterion I am said not to meet, quotes that criterion, and states which document it comes from, so that I can respond to it or pursue further review.

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-13, which is 180 days from the date of the denial notice, and I am submitting it before that date. I am sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter. I understand I may also file through ambetterhealth.com by selecting North Carolina and using that state's appeal or grievance form, or by calling the number on my member ID card.

Please contact me if you need anything further from me or from Dr. Okafor's office. I am glad to have additional records sent.

Thank you for your time and reconsideration.

Sincerely,

**Rowan Ellison**
